evidence: Independent regeneration using the committed gen.py/gogam.py algorithms gives 7436 Gog triangles and 7436 Magog triangles at n=6; all generated objects satisfy their validators.
Schützenberger images of all n=6 Magog triangles satisfy the implemented GOGAm inequality, and distinct left projections give 132, 1594, 4862 for k=1,2,3 on both sides.
The committed LGV routine gives 4862 for (m,n,k)=(0,6,3), agreeing with the exhaustive headline count.

Replacing that verifier with a self-contained committed-artifact verifier repairs reproducibility without changing the scientific headline.

Biane–Cheballah formulate left Gog/GOGAm equinumeration and provide explicit bijections for widths 1 and 2; targeted searches did not locate the exact finite width-3 (6,3) count 4862 in prior literature.
The audit claims novelty only for this finite computational checkpoint, not for the all-n width-3 conjecture.
A rigorously reproducible finite checkpoint in the first width beyond the explicitly solved width-1/2 cases is useful as regression data and a constraint for proposed all-n bijections.
The value is narrow but concrete; the record correctly avoids claiming the general conjecture.
